rules.title: Folder Naming Convention
rules.check: All folder names MUST use PascalCase (capital first letter). No lowercase folders.
rules.rationale: PascalCase folders match .NET namespace conventions and maintain consistency.

rules.title: Solution Structure
rules.check: Solutions MUST organize projects in standard folders: src/, tests/, optionally tools/, docs/.
rules.good_example:
MyApp.sln
src/
  MyApp.Api/
  MyApp.Core/
  MyApp.Infrastructure/
tests/
  MyApp.Api.Tests/
  MyApp.Core.Tests/
docs/
tools/
rules.rationale: Standard structure enables predictable navigation and build configurations.

rules.title: Project Naming
rules.check: Projects MUST follow Company.Product.Layer naming pattern.
rules.rationale: Qualified names prevent conflicts and clarify ownership.

rules.title: Domain-First Organization
rules.check: Organize by domain/feature, not by technical layer. No Features/ wrapper folder.
rules.bad_example:
Features/
  Orders/
  Users/
Controllers/
Services/
Repositories/
rules.good_example:
Orders/
  OrderController.cs
  OrderService.cs
  OrderRepository.cs
  OrderDto.cs
Users/
  UserController.cs
  UserService.cs
rules.rationale: Domain-first organization keeps related code together and reduces navigation.

rules.title: Primitives Project
rules.check: Shared base types MUST live in a *.Primitives or *.Contracts project with no dependencies.
rules.bad_example:
// Shared types scattered across projects
MyApp.Api/Models/EntityBase.cs
MyApp.Core/Common/Result.cs
MyApp.Infrastructure/Interfaces/IIdentifiable.cs
rules.good_example:
MyCompany.OrderSystem.Primitives/
  Entities/EntityBase.cs
  ValueObjects/Money.cs
  Interfaces/IIdentifiable.cs
  Results/Result.cs
  Enums/OrderStatus.cs
rules.rationale: Leaf dependency project prevents circular references and centralizes shared types.

rules.title: File-Type Matching
rules.check: File names MUST exactly match the primary type name.
rules.bad_example:
OrderModels.cs       // Contains Order class
UserServiceImpl.cs   // Contains UserService class
Dtos.cs              // Contains multiple DTOs
rules.good_example:
Order.cs             // Contains Order class
UserService.cs       // Contains UserService class
OrderDto.cs          // Contains OrderDto record
CreateOrderRequest.cs // Contains CreateOrderRequest record
rules.rationale: Predictable file names enable quick navigation and prevent confusion.

rules.title: One Primary Type Per File
rules.check: Each file MUST contain one primary public type. Related nested/helper types may coexist.
rules.rationale: Single-type files are easier to navigate, review, and maintain.

rules.title: Interface File Separation
rules.check: Interfaces MUST be in separate files from implementations. All interfaces in Interfaces/ folder.
rules.good_example:
Interfaces/
  IOrderService.cs
  IOrderRepository.cs
Services/
  OrderService.cs
Repositories/
  OrderRepository.cs
rules.rationale: Separate interface files enable dependency inversion and clean architecture.

rules.title: Related Records in Single File
rules.check: Small related records (DTOs, requests, responses) MAY share a file if closely related.
rules.bad_example:
// Too many unrelated types in one file
AllOrderDtos.cs // Contains 20 different DTOs
rules.rationale: Grouping related records reduces file count while maintaining cohesion.

rules.title: Extension Files
rules.check: Extension methods MUST be in Extensions/ folder with {Type}Extensions.cs naming.
rules.rationale: Consistent location and naming makes extensions discoverable.

rules.title: Configuration Files
rules.check: Configuration option classes MUST be in Configuration/ or Options/ folder.
rules.rationale: Centralized configuration is easier to review and maintain.

rules.title: Namespace-Folder Alignment
rules.check: Namespaces MUST match folder path. No namespace/folder mismatches.
rules.bad_example:
// File: src/Orders/Services/OrderService.cs
namespace MyApp.Services; // Doesn't match path
rules.rationale: Matching namespaces and folders prevents confusion and enables tooling.

rules.title: Test Project Structure
rules.check: Test projects MUST mirror source project structure.
rules.good_example:
MyApp.Core.Tests/
  Orders/
    OrderServiceTests.cs
    OrderValidatorTests.cs
  Users/
    UserServiceTests.cs
  Fixtures/
    DatabaseFixture.cs
  Helpers/
    TestDataBuilder.cs
rules.rationale: Parallel structure makes finding and maintaining tests intuitive.

rules.title: Project File Configuration
rules.check: All .csproj files MUST be explicit with full configuration, not minimal/implicit.
rules.good_example:
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
  <PropertyGroup>
    <!-- Build Configuration -->
    <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
    <Nullable>enable</Nullable>
    <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
    <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
    <WarningsAsErrors />

    <!-- Assembly Information -->
    <RootNamespace>MyCompany.OrderSystem.Api</RootNamespace>
    <AssemblyName>MyCompany.OrderSystem.Api</AssemblyName>

    <!-- Documentation -->
    <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
    <NoWarn>$(NoWarn);1591</NoWarn>

    <!-- Analyzers -->
    <EnableNETAnalyzers>true</EnableNETAnalyzers>
    <AnalysisLevel>latest</AnalysisLevel>
    <EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>true</EnforceCodeStyleInBuild>

    <!-- Package Metadata -->
    <Authors>MyCompany</Authors>
    <Company>MyCompany</Company>
    <Description>Order System API</Description>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!-- Dependencies -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi" Version="10.0.0" />
  </ItemGroup>

  <!-- Project References -->
  <ItemGroup>
    <ProjectReference Include="..\MyCompany.OrderSystem.Core\MyCompany.OrderSystem.Core.csproj" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
rules.rationale: Explicit configuration prevents surprises and documents project requirements.

rules.title: GlobalUsings File
rules.check: Common using statements MUST be in GlobalUsings.cs at project root.
rules.rationale: Global usings reduce repetition and ensure consistent imports.

rules.title: No lowercase folder names
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No lowercase folder names

rules.title: No `Features/` wrapper folder - use domain names directly
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No `Features/` wrapper folder - use domain names directly

rules.title: No multiple public types in single file (except records)
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No multiple public types in single file (except records)

rules.title: No namespace/folder mismatches
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No namespace/folder mismatches

rules.title: No `Helpers/` or `Utils/` as catch-all folders
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No `Helpers/` or `Utils/` as catch-all folders

rules.title: No `Misc/` or `Other/` folders
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No `Misc/` or `Other/` folders

rules.title: No deeply nested folders (max 5 levels from project root)
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No deeply nested folders (max 5 levels from project root)

rules.title: No minimal `.csproj` files without explicit configuration
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No minimal `.csproj` files without explicit configuration

rules.title: No business logic in `Common/` folders
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No business logic in `Common/` folders

rules.title: No mixed concerns in single folder
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No mixed concerns in single folder
